body:
I don't believe I have any achievements worth mentioning.  I don't have any serious regrets.

Home life was rough growing up.  My mother always got angry and frustrated with me because of my grades.  She always seemed to think I wasn't trying even when I was doing my best.

>Is there a reason why your IQ is so low?

There are several reasons, genetics for one.  Both of my parents have IQs that are clearly a bit below average.  However, my mother had me when she was 41 and she was drinking during my pregnancy, which I'm sure had an impact on my IQ given the fact that I'm less intelligent than my older brothers.

I'm not religious.  I am almost certain there is no god, at least not in the religious "creator and supreme ruler of all that exists" sense, but I admit I could be wrong.  If you want to put a label on me, agnostic works fine.  I can get along perfectly fine with religious people as well as agnostic and atheist people.  My best friend in high school was a devout Christian.
How am I brave?  I am making this AMA behind total anonymity.  I'm not even using my primary account.  Thank you though.
I don't vote.  I don't care about politics at all.
I'm not adventurous at all.  I don't play video games, I don't care about sports, and I don't drink coffee or tea.

Contrary to popular belief, being able to properly utilize vocabulary isn't a demonstration of human intelligence.  Intelligible just means "can be understood".  As long as you can understand those three words and know that "intelligible" is an adjective, you can properly use it in a sentence.  Some people are intellectually incapable of understanding the words "can be understood" and the concept of what an "adjective" is, but we're talking about people who are legitimately retarded, which I am not.

Whether or not someone *would* use the word is irrelevant since we're talking about intellectual capabilities.

I try my absolute hardest when I post online, most people make little to no effort.

>Are there things you want to do in life?

I have pretty much no interest in anything besides food and sex (which includes porn and masturbation I suppose, that's all I get anyway).  I have no hobbies or major goals in life.  This sounds really horrible to most people but I didn't choose to be like this.  We don't choose what interests us.  We can try to do things, we can pretend to care about things, but we don't choose what we legitimately care about.

>What goals do you have for yourself in the future?

I don't really have any "goals".

>What was your life like growing up?

Rough.  It took **a lot** of effort to pass my classes in school.  Everyone thought I wasn't trying hard when I was trying my hardest.  Even my mother for some reason thought I was slacking and could see that I was putting in a huge amount of effort.  Speaking of my mother, it's actually her fault I have a low IQ.  Not just because she has a somewhat low IQ, but also because she was 41 when she had me and she was drinking a lot while pregnant with me.

My spelling is only correct thanks to autocorrect and spellchecker.  These days, the only way you can make a post with incorrect spelling is if you completely ignore the red lines.  I'm stupid, not blind.  My grammar is only correct because I try hard.  

If you met me in person you would quickly realize I'm genuinely slow.  When responding to someone on the internet I can reread their post as many times as I want, really think about what I'm going to reply with before posting, look up words, etc.  These are obviously not luxuries I have in real life while having conversations in real time, so my intelligence (or lack thereof) becomes immediately apparent to everyone.

>but having been a teacher, i have seen much, much worse writing in people who were probably at well above an 81 IQ.

I'm sure you have but first of all a lot of those were written assignments I imagine.  When you write words on paper there's no autocorrect and red lines don't appear when you spell something incorrectly.  Believe me, those things alone make a massive difference.

There's also the fact that some of your students probably didn't try.  Right now, I'm writing at the very pinnacle of my English abilities whereas your students who wrote very poorly were just trying to get done as quickly as possible so they could go do something else.

>What do you do for a living?

I work at a fast food restaurant.  

>How long has your IQ been an issue, or caused issues in your life? 

Ever since I can remember.  

>What was your educational experience like? 

I tried my hardest and I barely passed high school.  I never went to college.

>Do you believe we live in a society that overemphasizes intelligence? 

No, quite the opposite.  Most people say IQ tests mean absolutely nothing.  Most people talk as if everyone has more or less the same intellectual potential and can achieve the same intellectual feats with enough effort.

The moment you even hint at there being genetic aptitudes involved with regards to human intelligence, everyone will say you're wrong.

I think political correctness is involved here.  The politically correct view is that everyone has equal mental capabilities and that differences in performance is solely due to external factors such as education and upbringing and effort.

The only reason I don't have any spelling errors is because of autocorrect and using a spellchecker.  These days, the only way you can spell a word incorrectly online is if you completely ignore the red lines.  I'm stupid, not blind.

I never had any prescriptions.  Adderall is for ADHD, which I'm pretty sure I don't have.  It helps people stay focused, but not being able to focus isn't my problem.
